description: The AutoCAD ActiveX (COM) object model used from VBA, VB.NET/C# COM interop, Python (win32com, pyautocad), PowerShell and AutoLISP vla- functions: Application and Documents, document-level methods (save, close, PostCommand, undo marks, purge, handles, export, wblock), plotting, layouts and preferences, entity creation methods of ModelSpace/PaperSpace, layers, block references and dynamic properties, selection sets with filters, entity editing methods, XData/XRecords, the Utility object and ObjectDBX. COM automation is not available in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: AcadDocuments.Open
tools.description: Opens an existing drawing in the running AutoCAD session and returns its Document object, optionally read-only. It is the entry point of most external automation scripts that process specific drawings through the editor.

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Full path of the DWG (or DWS/DXF).

parameters.name: ReadOnly
parameters.description: True to open read-only.

parameters.name: Password
parameters.description: Password for legacy encrypted drawings.

tools.example:
import win32com.client
acad = win32com.client.Dispatch("AutoCAD.Application")
doc = acad.Documents.Open(r"C:\Proj\A-101.dwg")
print(doc.Name, doc.ModelSpace.Count)
doc.Close(False)
tools.notes: Opening makes the document active, and COM calls block while AutoCAD is busy; retry on 'Call was rejected by callee' (RPC_E_CALL_REJECTED). For large batches prefer accoreconsole or ObjectDBX, which avoid editor overhead.

tools.name: AcadDocuments.Add
tools.description: Creates a new drawing, optionally from a template, and returns the new Document, which becomes the active document.

parameters.name: TemplateName
parameters.description: DWT name or path; defaults to the template set in Options (or acad.dwt).

tools.example:
Dim doc As AcadDocument
Set doc = ThisDrawing.Application.Documents.Add("acadiso.dwt")
doc.SaveAs "C:\Out\new_sheet.dwg"
tools.notes: Documents.Count and Documents.Item(i) enumerate open drawings; Documents.Close closes all of them.

tools.name: AcadDocument.SaveAs
tools.description: Saves the document to a new name and optionally in a different DWG/DXF version or as a template. After the call the document refers to the new file.

parameters.name: FullFileName
parameters.description: Target path including extension.

parameters.name: SaveAsType
parameters.description: AcSaveAsType: acNative, ac2018_dwg, ac2013_dwg, ac2010_dwg, ac2007_dwg, ac2018_dxf, ac2018_Template, ...

tools.example:
' down-save a copy for a consultant on an older release
ThisDrawing.SaveAs "C:\Out\A-101_R2013.dwg", ac2013_dwg
tools.notes: Use doc.Save for an in-place save. Saving to DXF switches the open document to the DXF file.

tools.name: AcadDocument.Close
tools.description: Closes a document, optionally saving changes and optionally under a new file name. Used at the end of each iteration of a batch loop.

parameters.name: SaveChanges
parameters.description: True to save (default prompts or saves depending on context), False to discard.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Save under this name when SaveChanges is True.

tools.example:
for f in files:
    d = acad.Documents.Open(f)
    d.PurgeAll()
    d.Close(True)
tools.notes: Closing the document that is running the VBA macro is not allowed; in VBA process other documents or use a separate launcher.

tools.name: AcadDocument.PostCommand
tools.description: Posts a command string to the document's command line for asynchronous processing. Unlike SendCommand, which processes the string before returning, PostCommand queues the input and returns immediately, which avoids re-entrancy problems when called from modeless code or event handlers.

parameters.name: Command
parameters.description: Command text; a space or vbCr at the end acts as Enter.

tools.example:
ThisDrawing.PostCommand "_.ZOOM _E "
ThisDrawing.PostCommand "(load ""stdtools.lsp"") "
tools.notes: Because execution is deferred, code after PostCommand cannot rely on the command having finished. Use Application.GetAcadState().IsQuiescent to wait from an external process.

tools.name: AcadDocument.StartUndoMark
tools.description: Starts an undo group so that all subsequent operations until EndUndoMark are undone as one step. Wrap every macro that performs several edits in StartUndoMark/EndUndoMark.

parameters.name: EndUndoMark
parameters.description: Closes the group; must always be called, including in error handlers.

tools.example:
Sub RecolorHatches()
  On Error GoTo done
  ThisDrawing.StartUndoMark
  Dim e As AcadEntity
  For Each e In ThisDrawing.ModelSpace
    If TypeOf e Is AcadHatch Then e.color = acByLayer
  Next
done:
  ThisDrawing.EndUndoMark
End Sub
tools.notes: Ignored when UNDO control is None or One.

tools.name: AcadDocument.PurgeAll
tools.description: Removes all unreferenced named objects (blocks, layers, linetypes, text and dimension styles, and so on) from the document, like PURGE All without prompts.

parameters.name: (none)
parameters.description: No arguments.

tools.example:
' repeat because purging a block can orphan layers it used
Dim i As Integer
For i = 1 To 3: ThisDrawing.PurgeAll: Next i
tools.notes: A single call does one pass; nested items become purgeable only on later passes. Zero-length geometry and empty text objects are not removed; use -PURGE with its Zero-length and Empty text options for those.

tools.name: AcadDocument.HandleToObject
tools.description: Returns the object that has a given handle string. Handles are persistent across sessions, so they are the right key for linking drawing objects to spreadsheets or databases.

parameters.name: Handle
parameters.description: Hexadecimal handle string, as returned by obj.Handle.

tools.example:
Dim obj As AcadEntity
Set obj = ThisDrawing.HandleToObject("2A7F")
obj.Highlight True
tools.notes: Raises an error if the handle does not exist or the object was erased; wrap in error handling. ObjectIdToObject converts a session ObjectID instead.

tools.name: AcadDocument.Export
tools.description: Exports objects of the drawing to another file format such as WMF, SAT, EPS, BMP or DXF. A selection set specifies the objects for most formats.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Target path without extension.

parameters.name: Extension
parameters.description: "WMF", "SAT", "EPS", "DXF" or "BMP".

parameters.name: SelectionSet
parameters.description: Objects to export (an empty set may be required for whole-drawing DXF).

tools.example:
Dim ss As AcadSelectionSet
Set ss = ThisDrawing.SelectionSets.Add("EXP")
ss.Select acSelectionSetAll
ThisDrawing.Export "C:\Out\solids", "SAT", ss
ss.Delete
tools.notes: PDF output is done through plotting (DWG To PDF.pc3) rather than Export.

tools.name: AcadDocument.Wblock
tools.description: Writes the objects in a selection set to a new drawing file, the ActiveX equivalent of WBLOCK with object selection.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: Output DWG path.

parameters.name: SelectionSet
parameters.description: Objects to write.

tools.example:
Dim ss As AcadSelectionSet
Set ss = ThisDrawing.SelectionSets.Add("WB")
ss.SelectOnScreen
ThisDrawing.Wblock "C:\Out\detail_5.dwg", ss
ss.Delete
tools.notes: Existing files are overwritten without warning. Named dependencies (layers, styles) used by the objects are included.

tools.name: AcadDocument.ActiveLayer
tools.description: Gets or sets the current layer as a Layer object. Sibling properties set the other drawing 'current' states: ActiveTextStyle, ActiveLinetype, ActiveDimStyle, ActiveLayout, ActiveSpace, ActiveUCS and ActiveViewport.

parameters.name: ActiveSpace
parameters.description: acModelSpace (1) or acPaperSpace (0).

parameters.name: MSpace
parameters.description: True to activate model space inside a layout viewport.

tools.example:
doc.ActiveLayer = doc.Layers.Item("A-ANNO")   # Python/win32com
doc.ActiveTextStyle = doc.TextStyles.Item("ISO")
tools.notes: Assigning a frozen layer as ActiveLayer raises an error; thaw it first.

tools.name: AcadPlot.PlotToFile
tools.description: Plots the active layout (or the layouts set with SetLayoutsToPlot) to a file, for example a PDF via the DWG To PDF.pc3 configuration. Returns True on success.

parameters.name: PlotFile
parameters.description: Output path (extension according to the device).

parameters.name: PlotConfig
parameters.description: Optional PC3 name overriding the layout's configured device.

parameters.name: SetLayoutsToPlot
parameters.description: Plot.SetLayoutsToPlot(array of layout names) before plotting several layouts.

tools.example:
ThisDrawing.SetVariable "BACKGROUNDPLOT", 0
With ThisDrawing.ActiveLayout
  .ConfigName = "DWG To PDF.pc3"
  .CanonicalMediaName = "ISO_full_bleed_A3_(420.00_x_297.00_MM)"
  .RefreshPlotDeviceInfo
End With
ThisDrawing.Plot.PlotToFile "C:\Out\A-101.pdf"
tools.notes: Set BACKGROUNDPLOT to 0, otherwise the call returns before the file is written. Plot.QuietErrorMode = True suppresses error dialogs in batch runs.

tools.name: AcadPlot.PlotToDevice
tools.description: Sends the active layout (or layouts set with SetLayoutsToPlot) to a printer or plotter, using the layout's page setup or an overriding PC3 configuration.

parameters.name: PlotConfig
parameters.description: Optional PC3 or Windows system printer name.

parameters.name: NumberOfCopies
parameters.description: Plot.NumberOfCopies before plotting.

tools.example:
ThisDrawing.Plot.NumberOfCopies = 2
ThisDrawing.Plot.PlotToDevice "\\PRINTSRV\A3-Colour"
tools.notes: Use Plot.DisplayPlotPreview acFullPreview for an interactive preview before plotting.

tools.name: AcadLayout.GetCanonicalMediaNames
tools.description: Returns the list of paper sizes (canonical media names) available for the layout's current plot device. Combined with ConfigName, CanonicalMediaName, PlotType, StandardScale, StyleSheet and PlotRotation it lets scripts build page setups.

parameters.name: ConfigName
parameters.description: Plot device (PC3 or system printer); set it and call RefreshPlotDeviceInfo before querying media.

parameters.name: GetLocaleMediaName
parameters.description: Translates a canonical name into the display name shown in dialogs.

parameters.name: GetPlotDeviceNames / GetPlotStyleTableNames
parameters.description: List available devices and CTB/STB tables.

tools.example:
lay = doc.ActiveLayout
lay.ConfigName = "DWG To PDF.pc3"
lay.RefreshPlotDeviceInfo()
for n in lay.GetCanonicalMediaNames():
    print(n, '->', lay.GetLocaleMediaName(n))
tools.notes: Canonical names are locale-independent and must be used when setting CanonicalMediaName.

tools.name: AcadPreferences.Files
tools.description: The PreferencesFiles object (Application.Preferences.Files) exposes the file-search settings of the Options dialog: SupportPath, PrinterConfigPath, PrinterStyleSheetPath, TemplateDwgPath, AutoSavePath, TempFilePath, FontFileMap and others. Other Preferences sub-objects cover Display, OpenSave, System, User, Drafting, Selection and Profiles.

parameters.name: SupportPath
parameters.description: Semicolon-separated support file search path.

parameters.name: TrustedPaths
parameters.description: Trusted locations for SECURELOAD (also via the TRUSTEDPATHS variable).

parameters.name: Preferences.Profiles
parameters.description: ActiveProfile, ImportProfile, ExportProfile, CopyProfile.

tools.notes: Changes are stored in the current profile in the registry and persist across sessions. Deployment tools often prefer .arg profile files.

tools.name: AcadApplication.ZoomExtents
tools.description: Zooms the active viewport of the active document to the drawing extents. The Application object also provides ZoomAll, ZoomWindow, ZoomCenter, ZoomScaled, ZoomPrevious and ZoomPickWindow.

parameters.name: LowerLeft / UpperRight
parameters.description: 3-element double arrays for ZoomWindow.

tools.example:
acad.ZoomExtents()
doc.Save()
tools.notes: Zoom affects the active document only; activate a document (doc.Activate) before zooming it.

tools.name: AcadApplication.GetAcadState
tools.description: Returns an AcadState object whose IsQuiescent property tells whether AutoCAD is idle (no active command, no pending input). External programs poll it before sending further COM calls or commands.
tools.usage:
Set st = acad.GetAcadState()
If st.IsQuiescent Then ...

parameters.name: IsQuiescent
parameters.description: True when AutoCAD is ready for new automation requests.

tools.example:
import time
doc.PostCommand("_.-PURGE _A * _N ")
while not acad.GetAcadState().IsQuiescent:
    time.sleep(0.2)
tools.notes: Polling with a short sleep avoids 'Call was rejected by callee' errors from out-of-process clients.

tools.name: AcadApplication.RunMacro
tools.description: Runs a VBA macro from a loaded or specified .dvb project. LoadDVB and UnloadDVB manage VBA projects, and LoadARX/UnloadARX/ListARX manage ObjectARX modules from automation clients.

parameters.name: MacroPath
parameters.description: [project.dvb!][module.]macro name.

parameters.name: LoadARX / LoadDVB
parameters.description: Full path of the module or project to load.

tools.example:
acad.LoadDVB(r"C:\CAD\VBA\tools.dvb")
acad.RunMacro("tools.dvb!Module1.ExportAttributes")
tools.notes: VBA requires the separately installed VBA module for AutoCAD. Macros cannot receive arguments; pass data through USERR/USERS system variables or files.

tools.name: AcadApplication.GetInterfaceObject
tools.description: Creates an instance of a COM object inside the AutoCAD process from its ProgID. Its main use is creating ObjectDBX documents (ObjectDBX.AxDbDocument.25 for the AutoCAD 2025/2026 family) and objects of vertical-product type libraries.

parameters.name: ProgID
parameters.description: E.g. "ObjectDBX.AxDbDocument.25" or "AutoCAD.AcCmColor.25"; the suffix follows the release family (24 for 2021-2024, 25 for 2025-2026).

tools.example:
Dim col As AcadAcCmColor
Set col = ThisDrawing.Application.GetInterfaceObject("AutoCAD.AcCmColor.25")
col.SetRGB 255, 128, 0
ent.TrueColor = col
tools.notes: The version suffix is a common source of 'Problem in loading application' errors after upgrades; derive it from Application.Version where possible.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AddLightWeightPolyline
tools.description: Creates a lightweight 2D polyline from an array of 2D vertex coordinates (x1, y1, x2, y2, ...). Closed, ConstantWidth, Elevation and bulges (SetBulge) are set on the returned object.

parameters.name: VerticesList
parameters.description: Array of doubles with an even number of values (at least 4).

tools.example:
import win32com.client, pythoncom
def darr(*v): return win32com.client.VARIANT(pythoncom.VT_ARRAY | pythoncom.VT_R8, v)
ms = acad.ActiveDocument.ModelSpace
pl = ms.AddLightWeightPolyline(darr(0, 0, 100, 0, 100, 50, 0, 50))
pl.Closed = True
tools.notes: From Python, coordinate arrays must be wrapped as VARIANT(VT_ARRAY|VT_R8); plain tuples raise type-mismatch errors. pyautocad's aDouble helper does the same.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.Add3DPoly
tools.description: Creates a 3D polyline from an array of 3D coordinates (x1, y1, z1, x2, y2, z2, ...). Used for survey strings, pipe centrelines and other non-planar polylines.

parameters.name: PointsArray
parameters.description: Array of doubles; length a multiple of 3, at least 6.

tools.example:
Dim pts(0 To 8) As Double
pts(0) = 0: pts(1) = 0: pts(2) = 0
pts(3) = 50: pts(4) = 0: pts(5) = 5
pts(6) = 50: pts(7) = 40: pts(8) = 12
ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.Add3DPoly pts
tools.notes: 3D polylines have no width or arcs. AppendVertex adds points later.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AddMText
tools.description: Creates a multiline text object at an insertion point with a boundary width and a text string that may include MText formatting codes.

parameters.name: InsertionPoint
parameters.description: 3-element double array.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: Boundary width; 0 for no wrapping.

parameters.name: Text
parameters.description: Content; \P for new paragraphs.

tools.example:
Dim p(0 To 2) As Double: p(0) = 10: p(1) = 200
Dim mt As AcadMText
Set mt = ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.AddMText(p, 120, "NOTES\PAll dimensions in mm.")
mt.Height = 3.5
mt.AttachmentPoint = acAttachmentPointTopLeft
tools.notes: In VBA the backslash needs no escaping; in Python use raw strings or doubled backslashes.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AddHatch
tools.description: Creates a Hatch object with a pattern and associativity setting; the boundary is then defined with AppendOuterLoop (and AppendInnerLoop for islands) and computed with Evaluate.
tools.usage:
Set h = ModelSpace.AddHatch(PatternType, PatternName, Associativity [, HatchObjectType])
h.AppendOuterLoop ObjectArray
h.Evaluate

parameters.name: PatternType
parameters.description: acHatchPatternTypePreDefined, acHatchPatternTypeUserDefined or acHatchPatternTypeCustomDefined.

parameters.name: PatternName
parameters.description: Pattern such as "ANSI31" or "SOLID".

parameters.name: Associativity
parameters.description: True to associate the hatch with its boundary objects.

parameters.name: HatchObjectType
parameters.description: acHatchObject (default) or acGradientObject.

tools.example:
Dim outer(0) As AcadEntity
Set outer(0) = boundaryPline
Dim h As AcadHatch
Set h = ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.AddHatch(acHatchPatternTypePreDefined, "ANSI31", True)
h.AppendOuterLoop outer
h.PatternScale = 2
h.Evaluate
tools.notes: Loops must be closed; the objects array must be declared As AcadEntity (or Object) for AppendOuterLoop to accept it.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AddDimAligned
tools.description: Creates an aligned dimension between two extension-line origins with the dimension text at a given location, using the current dimension style. Related methods: AddDimRotated, AddDimAngular, AddDimRadial, AddDimDiametric, AddDimOrdinate, AddDimArc.

parameters.name: ExtLine1Point / ExtLine2Point
parameters.description: Measured points (3-element arrays).

parameters.name: TextPosition
parameters.description: Location of the dimension line/text.

tools.example:
p1 = darr(0, 0, 0); p2 = darr(100, 0, 0); tp = darr(50, 10, 0)
dim = ms.AddDimAligned(p1, p2, tp)
dim.StyleName = "ISO-25"
tools.notes: The dimension is not associative with geometry; use DIMREASSOCIATE or the command-line DIM commands if associativity is required.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AddTable
tools.description: Creates a table object with a given number of rows and columns, row height and column width, using the current table style. Cells are filled with SetText, SetCellValue or SetCellValueFromText.
tools.usage: Set t = ModelSpace.AddTable(InsertionPoint, NumRows, NumColumns, RowHeight, ColWidth)

parameters.name: NumRows / NumColumns
parameters.description: Initial table size (title and header rows count).

parameters.name: RowHeight / ColWidth
parameters.description: Initial sizes in drawing units.

tools.example:
Dim t As AcadTable
Set t = ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.AddTable(pt, 5, 3, 8, 40)
t.SetText 0, 0, "DOOR SCHEDULE"
t.SetText 1, 0, "Tag": t.SetText 1, 1, "Width": t.SetText 1, 2, "Height"
tools.notes: Rows and columns are zero-based. Call RegenerateTableSuppressed = True while filling large tables and set it back to False at the end for speed.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AddBox
tools.description: Creates a 3D solid box of given length (X), width (Y) and height (Z). The Origin argument is the center of the box, not a corner. Other solid primitives: AddCone, AddCylinder, AddSphere, AddTorus, AddWedge, AddExtrudedSolid, AddRevolvedSolid.
tools.usage: Set s = ModelSpace.AddBox(Origin, Length, Width, Height)

parameters.name: Origin
parameters.description: Center of the box (3-element array).

parameters.name: Length / Width / Height
parameters.description: Dimensions along X, Y, Z.

tools.example:
Dim c(0 To 2) As Double: c(0) = 50: c(1) = 30: c(2) = 10
Dim b As Acad3DSolid
Set b = ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.AddBox(c, 100, 60, 20)
b.Boolean acSubtraction, ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.AddCylinder(c, 5, 20)
tools.notes: Solid creation is not available in AutoCAD LT. 3DSolid.Boolean performs union/subtraction/intersection with another solid.

tools.name: AcadModelSpace.AttachExternalReference
tools.description: Attaches (or overlays) an external DWG reference at an insertion point with scale and rotation, returning an ExternalReference object.
tools.usage: Set x = ModelSpace.AttachExternalReference(PathName, Name, InsertionPoint, XScale, YScale, ZScale, Rotation, bOverlay [, Password])

parameters.name: PathName
parameters.description: Path of the referenced drawing (relative paths are resolved against the host drawing).

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Block name for the xref definition.

parameters.name: bOverlay
parameters.description: True for overlay, False for attachment.

tools.example:
Dim o(0 To 2) As Double
ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.AttachExternalReference _
  "..\Base\site.dwg", "SITE", o, 1, 1, 1, 0, True
tools.notes: Reload or detach through the Blocks collection: ThisDrawing.Blocks("SITE").Reload / .Detach.

tools.name: AcadPaperSpace.AddPViewport
tools.description: Creates a layout (paper-space) viewport with a center point, width and height. The viewport must be turned on with Display True, then its scale and view are set through StandardScale/CustomScale, ViewCenter and Direction.
tools.usage:
Set vp = PaperSpace.AddPViewport(Center, Width, Height)
vp.Display True

parameters.name: Center
parameters.description: Center point on the sheet (3-element array).

parameters.name: Width / Height
parameters.description: Viewport size in paper units.

parameters.name: StandardScale / CustomScale
parameters.description: acVp1_100 etc. or a numeric scale factor.

tools.example:
ThisDrawing.ActiveSpace = acPaperSpace
Dim c(0 To 2) As Double: c(0) = 210: c(1) = 148
Dim vp As AcadPViewport
Set vp = ThisDrawing.PaperSpace.AddPViewport(c, 380, 250)
vp.Display True
vp.StandardScale = acVpCustomScale: vp.CustomScale = 1 / 50
tools.notes: Viewports added to a layout that is not active may not display until the layout is activated. Lock the display with DisplayLocked.

tools.name: AcadLayer
tools.description: Layer object in the Layers collection with properties Name, Color/TrueColor, Linetype, Lineweight, LayerOn, Freeze, Lock, Plottable, Description, Transparency and Material, plus Delete. Created with Layers.Add(name).
tools.usage:
Set lay = doc.Layers.Add("E-POWER")
lay.Color = acRed: lay.Linetype = "DASHED": lay.Lock = False

parameters.name: Freeze / LayerOn / Lock
parameters.description: Visibility and edit state booleans.

parameters.name: Linetype
parameters.description: Name of a loaded linetype (load with doc.Linetypes.Load).

parameters.name: Lineweight
parameters.description: AcLineWeight constant such as acLnWt035.

tools.example:
lay = doc.Layers.Add("E-POWER")
if "DASHED" not in [lt.Name for lt in doc.Linetypes]:
    doc.Linetypes.Load("DASHED", "acadiso.lin")
lay.Linetype = "DASHED"
lay.Color = 1
tools.notes: Setting Freeze on the active layer raises an error. Layers.GenerateUsageData followed by layer.Used tells whether a layer is in use before deleting it.

tools.name: AcadBlockReference.GetAttributes
tools.description: Returns an array of the editable AttributeReference objects of a block reference, allowing attribute values to be read and changed (TagString, TextString). Constant attributes are returned by GetConstantAttributes.

parameters.name: HasAttributes
parameters.description: Check this property first; blocks without attributes return an empty array.

tools.notes: Iterating ModelSpace from Python is slow for large drawings (one COM round trip per object); filter with a SelectionSet first.

tools.name: AcadBlockReference.GetDynamicBlockProperties
tools.description: Returns the DynamicBlockReferenceProperty objects of a dynamic block reference, each with PropertyName, Value, AllowedValues, ReadOnly, UnitsType and Description. Setting Value changes the dynamic parameter.

parameters.name: IsDynamicBlock
parameters.description: Test before calling.

parameters.name: Value
parameters.description: Variant; must match the parameter type (Double for linear/angular, String for visibility).

parameters.name: EffectiveName
parameters.description: Original block name of a modified dynamic block.

tools.example:
Dim p As Variant, i As Integer
p = br.GetDynamicBlockProperties
For i = LBound(p) To UBound(p)
  If p(i).PropertyName = "Visibility1" Then p(i).Value = "Double door"
  If p(i).PropertyName = "Width" Then p(i).Value = CDbl(900)
Next i
tools.notes: Passing an Integer instead of Double for a distance raises 'Invalid input'. The Origin property is always read-only.

tools.name: AcadSelectionSet.Select
tools.description: Adds objects to a selection set without user interaction using a mode (window, crossing, previous, last, all) and optional filter arrays. FilterType holds DXF group codes and FilterData the matching values, like an ssget filter list.
tools.usage: ss.Select Mode [, Point1] [, Point2] [, FilterType, FilterData]

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: acSelectionSetWindow, acSelectionSetCrossing, acSelectionSetPrevious, acSelectionSetLast, acSelectionSetAll.

parameters.name: FilterType
parameters.description: Integer array of DXF codes (0 type, 8 layer, 2 block name, -4 operators).

parameters.name: FilterData
parameters.description: Variant array of values paired with FilterType.

tools.example:
Dim ft(1) As Integer, fd(1) As Variant
ft(0) = 0: fd(0) = "INSERT"
ft(1) = 2: fd(1) = "DOOR*"
Dim ss As AcadSelectionSet
Set ss = ThisDrawing.SelectionSets.Add("DOORS")
ss.Select acSelectionSetAll, , , ft, fd
MsgBox ss.Count & " doors"
ss.Delete
tools.notes: Selection set names must be unique; delete leftovers from a previous run. From Python, build FilterType as VARIANT(VT_ARRAY|VT_I2) and FilterData as VARIANT(VT_ARRAY|VT_VARIANT).

tools.name: AcadSelectionSet.SelectOnScreen
tools.description: Prompts the user to select objects on screen and adds them to the selection set, optionally with the same FilterType/FilterData filtering as Select.

parameters.name: FilterType / FilterData
parameters.description: Optional DXF filter arrays.

tools.example:
Dim ft(0) As Integer, fd(0) As Variant
ft(0) = 0: fd(0) = "TEXT,MTEXT"
Set ss = ThisDrawing.SelectionSets.Add("TXT")
ss.SelectOnScreen ft, fd
tools.notes: In external (out-of-process) automation the AutoCAD window must be activated for the user to pick; the call blocks until selection ends.

tools.name: AcadSelectionSet.SelectByPolygon
tools.description: Selects objects using a fence, window polygon or crossing polygon defined by a list of points, with optional filters. Useful for selecting everything inside a room outline or crossing a route.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: acSelectionSetFence, acSelectionSetWindowPolygon or acSelectionSetCrossingPolygon.

parameters.name: PointsList
parameters.description: Array of doubles with 3D coordinates (x, y, z per point).

tools.example:
' select all blocks inside a closed polyline's outline
Dim c As Variant: c = pline.Coordinates   ' 2D list x,y,...
Dim pts() As Double, i As Long, n As Long
n = (UBound(c) + 1) / 2
ReDim pts(0 To n * 3 - 1)
For i = 0 To n - 1: pts(i * 3) = c(i * 2): pts(i * 3 + 1) = c(i * 2 + 1): Next
ss.SelectByPolygon acSelectionSetWindowPolygon, pts
tools.notes: Like interactive polygon selection, only objects visible on screen are reliably found; zoom to the area first.

tools.name: AcadEntity.Move
tools.description: Moves an entity by the vector from Point1 to Point2. The editing family on every entity also includes Copy (returns the copy), Rotate (base point, angle in radians), ScaleEntity (base point, factor), Mirror (returns the mirrored copy), Rotate3D, Mirror3D, TransformBy and Delete.
tools.usage:
ent.Move Point1, Point2
Set c = ent.Copy()
ent.Rotate BasePoint, RotationAngle
ent.ScaleEntity BasePoint, ScaleFactor
Set m = ent.Mirror(Point1, Point2)

parameters.name: Point1 / Point2
parameters.description: 3-element arrays defining the displacement.

parameters.name: RotationAngle
parameters.description: Radians, counterclockwise.

tools.example:
from math import radians
new = ent.Copy()
new.Move(darr(0, 0, 0), darr(0, 500, 0))
new.Rotate(darr(0, 500, 0), radians(90))
tools.notes: Mirror leaves the original in place; delete it if you want MIRROR with 'erase source'. MIRRTEXT affects text mirroring.

tools.name: AcadEntity.ArrayRectangular
tools.description: Creates a classic (non-associative) rectangular array of an entity and returns the new objects. ArrayPolar creates a polar array around a center point.
tools.usage:
objs = ent.ArrayRectangular(NumberOfRows, NumberOfColumns, NumberOfLevels, DistBetweenRows, DistBetweenCols, DistBetweenLevels)
objs = ent.ArrayPolar(NumberOfObjects, AngleToFill, CenterPoint)

parameters.name: NumberOfRows / Columns / Levels
parameters.description: Counts including the original (levels = 1 for 2D).

parameters.name: AngleToFill
parameters.description: ArrayPolar fill angle in radians (2*pi for a full circle).

tools.example:
Dim a As Variant
a = hole.ArrayRectangular(3, 4, 1, 25, 40, 0)
MsgBox (UBound(a) + 1) & " copies created"
tools.notes: These methods create separate objects; associative arrays (ARRAYRECT) are not exposed through ActiveX.

tools.name: AcadEntity.IntersectWith
tools.description: Returns the intersection points of two entities as a flat array of doubles (x, y, z per point). The extend option allows intersections with extended geometry.

parameters.name: IntersectObject
parameters.description: The other entity.

parameters.name: ExtendOption
parameters.description: acExtendNone, acExtendThisEntity, acExtendOtherEntity, acExtendBoth.

tools.example:
Dim v As Variant
v = line1.IntersectWith(line2, acExtendNone)
If VarType(v) <> vbEmpty Then
  If UBound(v) >= 2 Then Debug.Print v(0), v(1), v(2)
End If
tools.notes: No intersection returns an empty array (UBound = -1); always check the bounds before reading points.

tools.name: AcadEntity.GetBoundingBox
tools.description: Returns the minimum and maximum corners of the entity's WCS axis-aligned bounding box through two output arguments.

parameters.name: MinPoint / MaxPoint
parameters.description: Variant output arguments receiving 3-element arrays.

tools.example:
Dim mn As Variant, mx As Variant
ent.GetBoundingBox mn, mx
ThisDrawing.Application.ZoomWindow mn, mx
tools.notes: In Python/win32com output arguments are returned as a tuple: mn, mx = ent.GetBoundingBox().

tools.name: AcadObject.SetXData
tools.description: Attaches extended data (XData) to any object from two parallel arrays of group codes and values; GetXData reads it back for a given application name. The first pair must be code 1001 with a registered application name.
tools.usage:
obj.SetXData XDataType, XDataValue
obj.GetXData AppName, XDataType, XDataValue

parameters.name: XDataType
parameters.description: Integer array: 1001 app name, 1000 string, 1040 real, 1070 short, 1071 long, 1010 point ...

parameters.name: XDataValue
parameters.description: Variant array with the values.

parameters.name: AppName
parameters.description: For GetXData: application name, "" for all.

tools.example:
ThisDrawing.RegisteredApplications.Add "ACME"
Dim t(0 To 2) As Integer, v(0 To 2) As Variant
t(0) = 1001: v(0) = "ACME"
t(1) = 1000: v(1) = "PUMP-07"
t(2) = 1040: v(2) = 3.2
ent.SetXData t, v
Dim rt As Variant, rv As Variant
ent.GetXData "ACME", rt, rv
tools.notes: XData is limited to about 16 KB per object. SelectionSet filters on code -3 select objects carrying a given application's XData.

tools.name: AcadXRecord.SetXRecordData
tools.description: Stores arbitrary data in an XRecord created with Dictionary.AddXRecord, using parallel arrays of DXF group codes and values. GetXRecordData reads it back. Used for drawing-level application settings.
tools.usage:
Set dict = doc.Dictionaries.Add("ACME")
Set xr = dict.AddXRecord("SETTINGS")
xr.SetXRecordData XRecordDataType, XRecordData

parameters.name: XRecordDataType
parameters.description: Integer array of DXF codes (1 string, 40 real, 70 short, 90 long...).

parameters.name: XRecordData
parameters.description: Variant array of values.

tools.example:
Dim d As AcadDictionary, x As AcadXRecord
Set d = ThisDrawing.Dictionaries.Add("ACME")
Set x = d.AddXRecord("SETTINGS")
Dim t(0 To 1) As Integer, v(0 To 1) As Variant
t(0) = 1: v(0) = "Project 2026-017"
t(1) = 40: v(1) = 50#
x.SetXRecordData t, v
tools.notes: Dictionaries.Add returns the existing dictionary if the name exists. Per-object data goes into the object's extension dictionary (GetExtensionDictionary).

tools.name: AcadUtility.GetPoint
tools.description: Prompts the user for a point on screen (with optional rubber-band base point) and returns it as a WCS 3-element array. The Utility object also provides GetEntity, GetString, GetReal, GetInteger, GetDistance, GetAngle, GetKeyword, GetCorner, Prompt and InitializeUserInput.

parameters.name: Point
parameters.description: Optional base point for the rubber-band line (WCS).

parameters.name: Prompt
parameters.description: Prompt text.

parameters.name: InitializeUserInput
parameters.description: Call first to set bits (1 = no null) and keywords.

tools.example:
Dim p1 As Variant, p2 As Variant
p1 = ThisDrawing.Utility.GetPoint(, vbCrLf & "First point: ")
p2 = ThisDrawing.Utility.GetPoint(p1, vbCrLf & "Second point: ")
ThisDrawing.ModelSpace.AddLine p1, p2
tools.notes: Pressing Esc raises a run-time error, so use On Error handling. Unlike AutoLISP getpoint, the returned point is already in WCS.

tools.name: AcadUtility.TranslateCoordinates
tools.description: Converts a point or displacement between coordinate systems: WCS, UCS, display (DCS), paper-space DCS and an entity's OCS. The ActiveX equivalent of AutoLISP trans.
tools.usage: newPt = doc.Utility.TranslateCoordinates(Point, FromCoordSystem, ToCoordSystem, Displacement [, OCSNormal])

parameters.name: From/ToCoordSystem
parameters.description: acWorld, acUCS, acDisplayDCS, acPaperSpaceDCS or acOCS.

parameters.name: Displacement
parameters.description: True to treat the input as a vector (no translation).

parameters.name: OCSNormal
parameters.description: Normal of the OCS when acOCS is used.

tools.example:
Dim ucsPt As Variant
ucsPt = ThisDrawing.Utility.TranslateCoordinates(wcsPt, acWorld, acUCS, False)
tools.notes: Lightweight polyline and 2D entity coordinates are in OCS; translate with the entity's Normal before comparing with WCS points.

tools.name: ObjectDBX.AxDbDocument
tools.description: An in-memory drawing document created with Application.GetInterfaceObject("ObjectDBX.AxDbDocument.25") that opens DWG files without loading them into the editor. It exposes most of the Document object model (ModelSpace, Blocks, Layers, Layouts) and SaveAs, making batch reading and editing of many files fast.
tools.usage:
Set dbx = acad.GetInterfaceObject("ObjectDBX.AxDbDocument.25")
dbx.Open FileName [, Password]
' ... work ...
dbx.SaveAs FileName

parameters.name: Open
parameters.description: Loads a DWG into the ObjectDBX document.

parameters.name: SaveAs
parameters.description: Saves changes (there is no Save or Close method).

parameters.name: ProgID suffix
parameters.description: Matches the release family (24 for 2021-2024, 25 for 2025-2026).

tools.example:
(setq dbx (vla-GetInterfaceObject (vlax-get-acad-object) "ObjectDBX.AxDbDocument.25"))
(foreach f (vl-directory-files "C:/Proj" "*.dwg" 1)
  (vla-Open dbx (strcat "C:/Proj/" f))
  (vlax-for lay (vla-get-Layers dbx) (if (= (vla-get-Name lay) "TEMP") (vla-put-Freeze lay :vlax-true)))
  (vla-SaveAs dbx (strcat "C:/Proj/" f)))
(vlax-release-object dbx)
tools.notes: No editor: no commands, selection sets, SendCommand, zoom or text alignment adjustment; attribute alignment may need fixing after edits. Files open elsewhere cannot be saved. Release the object when done.
